model.rationale: Dave Min combines incumbency, a D-leaning seat, and a roughly seven-to-one cash advantage over Jenny Le Roux, while markets price his win odds near 96 percent; with no polling available, those fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic margin.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing a single-digit race or a late wave of Republican outside spending would move this toward Likely D.

overview:
Dave Min, the Democratic incumbent, seeks a second term in a district that leans Democratic by six points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $3.8 million and holding roughly $1.7 million on hand, while Republican Jenny Le Roux has raised about $553,000 with $155,000 available. Outside spending on either side has been negligible, and no independent groups have engaged in the race in a meaningful way.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both put Min's chances at about 96 percent. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the fundraising gap. Those factors point to a comfortable Democratic margin, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact size of the lead.
